Let's dive into Chapter 9: Creating Generational Impact and Legacy.
When you think about true kingdom wealth, it's not just about what you have right now—it’s really about building a legacy that’ll bless the generations that come after you.
That means looking beyond what you need today, and asking, “How will the choices I make now open up new opportunities for my children, and even their children?”
Legacy always starts with vision. So, what kind of impact do you genuinely want to leave behind?
Maybe you’re thinking about a financial inheritance. But legacy is so much more than that. It’s about passing on your values, your wisdom, and your relationships.
If you look at the stories in the Bible, you’ll see how much emphasis is placed on handing down faith, character, and a sense of purpose—not just material things.
So, how do you actually build a legacy that lasts? Let’s break it down:
First, model wise stewardship. Kids and the people around you will pick up far more from what you do than what you say. Show them what generosity, integrity, and hard work look like in everyday life.
Next, teach financial principles. Talk openly with your family and community about budgeting, saving, giving, and investing. The more you share, the more capable they’ll be in the future.
Third, plan for the future. Take steps like creating a will, setting up a trust, or using whatever tools you need so your resources get used exactly as you intend.
And finally, invest in people. Mentor someone. Encourage your kids or others to discover their purpose and reach their potential. Sometimes, the most lasting impact you’ll have is through a simple word of encouragement.
Think about this: families that have open conversations about money, that practice generosity, and actually involve their kids in giving decisions, they’re the ones who see those values naturally carried forward into the next generation.
The same goes for business owners. If you’re someone who puts effort into developing your employees and caring about the community, your influence will last way longer than any financial success alone.
And remember—legacy isn’t just about wealth. It’s about the stories you tell, the lives you touch, and the example you set. When you live with intention and keep an eye on the bigger picture, you’ll create ripples of blessing that go far beyond your own lifetime.
Here’s something to keep in mind, especially when times get tough: if your decisions are driven by a long-term vision, it becomes so much easier to stay focused through setbacks and not lose sight of what really matters.
In the end, creating generational impact is all about stewardship at the highest level—using what you have today to build a better future for others. It’s a journey powered by faith, wisdom, and love, and there’s real joy in watching the seeds you plant now bear fruit for many years to come.
